Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the private deployment and the KMS integrations look promising for our regulated workflows. After an internal review, the Procurement and Technical teams asked me to put a clear ask on pricing/packaging so we can move toward an LOI.

Quick summary of the request:
- Redwood Private (VPC) with dedicated capacity for production (3x gpus equivalent)
- 12-month commitment; target start Aug 1
- Requesting a one-time commercial concession of 42% off list on the committed capacity for the first 6 months, plus a 12% discount on overage rates
- Seeking a 12-month rate lock and dedicated support (SLA + 8x5) included

We understand this is material, so please escalate as needed — the Procurement team asked for VP/CFO review and a short exec memo outlining margin impact and any guardrails you’d want in the contract. We can accept step-downs or milestone-based price reversion if that helps.

I’ve attached our internal term sheet (v2) to make it concrete. Happy to schedule a call if you’d prefer to walk through the numbers.

Best,

Team — forwarding SynthMed’s ask. They’re strategic in the healthcare vertical and already have compliance requirements that map well to our Private offering.

Quick take / asks:
- Their headline: 42% off committed capacity for 6 months + 12% off overages, 12-month rate lock. That’s significantly higher than our guardrails.
- Attached margin calc shows estimated gross margin delta (~-9% on expected ARR for first year) if we accept as-is. I attached a draft Impact spreadsheet (Margin-Impact-Calc-20260713.xlsx).

Possible counter I’d propose for exec signoff:
1) 25% concession on committed capacity for first 6 months (not 42%)
2) 12-month rate lock honored only on committed volumes; overages billed at standard rates and subject to a 6% limited overage discount for the first quarter
3) Implementation fee of $50k to cover onboarding and compliance validation (non-refundable)
4) Include a 6-mo milestone clause that re-evaluates pricing if usage >1.5x forecast

If you’re comfortable with a path, can one of you draft a one-page executive approval memo for Markus with the margin numbers and recommended conditions? I’ll bring SynthMed onto a 30-minute call for final alignment once we have a signoff path.

Thanks for the head’s up, Dylan. I ran the numbers and pulled together a short exec brief (attached: Executive-Approval-Brief-20260714.pdf). Key points:

- Strategic rationale: SynthMed is a strong reference for regulated healthcare; having them on Redwood Private improves our vertical credibility and opens up a potential pipeline of similar accounts.
- Margin impact: The full 42% ask produces an unacceptable gross margin erosion (~-9% on projected Year 1). The proposed counter (25% + $50k onboarding fee + milestone re-eval) recovers ~60% of the downside and preserves commercial momentum.
- Risk controls we should insist on before approval: step-down after 6 months back to standard list unless usage ramp >= 1.2x forecast; non-refundable onboarding fee; accelerated billing for committed minimums; clear termination liability for early pull-out.

Recommendation (for Markus): Approve the counter under two conditions — (1) discount limited to committed volumes only and tied to an explicit milestone clause, (2) include a 12-month minimum committed ARR with accelerated billing cadence. I’ve put suggested contract language in the attached brief.

If Markus is comfortable, I’ll route the DocuSign-ready term sheet (with redlines) and Dylan can re-engage procurement to close.

-Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the analysis. I’m prepared to sign off to preserve the strategic motion, subject to firm guardrails. Approve the counteroffer as written by Marissa with the following binding conditions:

1) Discount applies to committed volumes only (documented in SOW). Overages billed at list, with an initial 6% temporary concession for Q1 post-go-live only.
2) Non-refundable onboarding fee ($50k) must be paid at contract signing.
3) 12-month minimum committed ARR with accelerated invoices for the first 3 billing cycles (to protect cash).
4) Include a six-month operational milestone review clause; if usage exceeds forecast by >20% we trigger a negotiated reprice. If usage is under 80% of forecast after 6 months, we reserve the right to recalibrate pricing unilaterally.
5) Legal to include an explicit revenue recognition and audit clause to avoid carveouts.

Kimberly — please prepare the approval memo and update the Margin-Impact spreadsheet to reflect these guardrails (I want final margin after onboarding fee amortization). Once that’s in doc form, route to me and I’ll sign the exec approval. Dylan — please hold off on any verbal commitments until DocuSign is prepared.

-Markus Klein
